newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $69, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $69, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle were bid $69.00 per cwt by a few packers but passed by owners pricing cattle at $70.00, feedlot sources said.
The bids were steady with this week's top of $69.00 attained in active trading Tuesday and Wednesday. This week's sales were $3.00 higher than last week's top price.
Gains were powered by strong beef prices and declining showlist numbers, the sources said.
Feedlot cattle next week were seen priced at $71.00 to $72.00 by owners anticipating further beef strength and diminished supplies of finished cattle, they said.

A few loads of cattle sold at $70.00 in western Nebraska on Wednesday, which generated expectations that feedlot sales in the Panhandle and Kansas would be at least $70.00 next week, and possibly higher, sources said.
Beef prices Thursday were quoted up $1.30 to $1.63 per cwt on 164 fabricated loads sold.
Heavier weight choice beef prices on Thursday rose $1.34 to $105.96 per cwt -- a $8.58 jump from a week earlier, USDA statistics showed.
